solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Show clears up act for broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters of the three words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre company tidies up its act before it goes out on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' signals the anagram of CLEARSUPACT; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A show as a noun can be a lavish television production, often called a spectacular.

clue.text: Stand-in on bed creating a minor story

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or stand-in
a garden bed is a plot of ground

explanation.surface: An understudy lying on a bed sets off a small side story.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary storyline running alongside the main plot of a novel or play.

clue.text: Attempt a bit of personality assessment on the way up

indicators.note: on the way up, in a down clue, says the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
a bit of says only a small run of letters inside these words is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a little of a personality test as they climb the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Attempt a bit' as the definition, but 'a bit of' is the hidden-word indicator, so the definition is 'Attempt' alone. 'on the way up' turns YASSE, found across 'personality assessment'.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt or trial, as in essaying a difficult task.

clue.text: People who malign dealers importing duck without wings

indicators.note: importing means bringing something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: traders are dealers in goods

indicators.note: a bird without wings loses its sides, so the outer letters of the word duck go

explanation.surface: Bad-mouthing merchants smuggle in a flightless bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without wings' clips both ends of the bird to leave UC, and 'importing' takes it into the dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to slander, so traducers are those who speak ill of others.

clue.text: Dock policeman covering river

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the policeman goes around the river

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: An officer patrols the docks beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a harbour noun, but it is the verb meaning to cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail or hair is to cut it short, the same as cropping it.

clue.text: A source of problems in poor golfer's game

indicators.note: in places the A and the first letter inside the rearranged letters
poor suggests something badly done, so the letters of golfer are scrambled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bad golfer's round is full of trouble from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the golfer to LEFROG, and 'in' puts the A plus P, from problems, into that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground game in which players vault over one another's bent backs.

clue.text: People who can be relied on to get shakes

definitions.text: People who can be relied on
definitions.meaning: dependable people are called someone's rock
to shake something is to rock it back and forth

explanation.surface: Trustworthy people end up trembling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks are steady, dependable people, and to rock is to shake or sway.

clue.text: Surprise, seeing Sun let loose

parts.note: the Sun is a star

indicators.note: set loose, the letters of let are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: A loose Sun would be astonishing to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges LET to TLE; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden surprise or fright.

clue.text: Figure straddling single bed is poison

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so the figure goes around the other pieces

parts.note: nine is a figure or number
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A form lying across a single bed turns out to be toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straddling' has the figure sitting astride the single and the bed, which sit between its first and second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is a toxic alkaloid found in tobacco, used historically as an insecticide.

clue.text: Dance leader with a star flaring up

parts.note: the boss is the one in charge
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: The head of the troupe and a sparkling star take to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian style of music and dance blending samba with jazz.

clue.text: Feature origin of African country

parts.note: a facial feature such as the chin

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trait traced back to the beginnings of an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A large nation in East Asia, the world's second most populous.

clue.text: Sailor leaves idler to spend

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the sailor is taken out

parts.note: a layabout is an idle person
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman walks out on a lazy man and goes off to splash his cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes AB from LAYABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out money is a phrasal verb meaning to spend it.

clue.text: Not working with film derivative

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working
to shoot is to film

explanation.surface: A dud with a camera produces something unoriginal.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is something that has developed from a larger thing, a spin-off.

clue.text: Changed course due to careful handling, say

indicators.note: say marks that the word is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: tact is sensitivity in dealing with delicate situations

explanation.surface: A ship altered direction because of skilful steering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' is a link; TACT and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat tacks when it changes course by turning its bow through the wind.

clue.text: Big girl's up, finding love after pass

indicators.note: after places love behind the pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a lass is a girl; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A girl is excited to find love after getting through her exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LASS to SSAL; 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous, like the giant statue the Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Abandoned pit, chasing good source of profit

indicators.note: chasing means running after, so the abandoned pit comes after the good

parts.note: an abandoned thing is old and disused
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: Prospectors pursue a good find in a disused colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold mine figuratively is anything that brings in great profit.

clue.text: Ruthless competition to follow trail across limitless heath

indicators.note: across says the pursuing pieces stretch over the heath piece, which sits between them

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
to trail someone is to dog them

indicators.note: limitless means without its outer limits, so the first and last letters of heath go

explanation.surface: Hounds track a scent over open moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless' strips H and H from HEATH to leave EAT, which sits between the two DOGs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eat-dog world is one of fierce, merciless rivalry.

clue.text: Shadow barmen up for replacement

indicators.note: replacement means swapping things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bar staff are summoned to be swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' rearranges BARMENUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The penumbra is the partly shaded outer region of a shadow, as in an eclipse.

clue.text: Black sticky stuff from a ship inside breakwaters

indicators.note: inside places the ship within the breakwaters

parts.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: Treacle is unloaded from a vessel moored within the harbour walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark thick syrup left from refining sugar, akin to treacle.

clue.text: Bishop with saint in Rome worried mafia type

indicators.note: in places the bishop and saint inside the rearranged city
worried means disturbed, so the letters of Rome are stirred up

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a holy man in the Italian capital fret about a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges ROME to MOER, and 'in' puts BST inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster is a gangster, a member of organised crime such as the Mafia.

clue.text: Birds, for example rest in flight

indicators.note: in flight suggests scattering, so the letters of rest are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some birds rest even while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in flight' rearranges REST to RETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons, a kind of wading bird.

clue.text: Level of society putting up 'Loose Women' with show of hesitation

indicators.note: putting up, in a down clue, says the word is raised and read backwards

parts.note: tarts is a slang term for promiscuous women
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A social class hesitantly hosts a daytime talk show.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose Women is a British daytime TV chat show, which is why it is quoted. 'putting up' turns TARTS to STRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer or class within society.

clue.text: Tried hard, however, welcoming upper-class investor

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: but means however
a stag is a speculator who buys new shares to sell quickly

explanation.surface: Someone made a great effort to welcome a posh financier.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag in City slang buys new share issues to sell at a quick profit; 'welcoming' takes the investor and the posh letter into however.
explanation.definitionFit: To bust a gut is an idiom for making a huge effort.

clue.text: Leading area hotel has regulars in demand

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: regulars are evenly spaced letters, here every other letter of demand

explanation.surface: A hotel in the area has regular guests in great demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulars in' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of DEMAND, EAD; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ahead is to be in front, leading a race or contest.

clue.text: Heap fury on bishop

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the fury after the bishop

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
anger is fury

explanation.surface: Pour rage on a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heap' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: an old wreck of a car, which British slang also calls a banger.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a dilapidated old car.

clue.text: Fertiliser rejected during season (August)

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run is read backwards
during says the letters sit within the run of words

explanation.surface: Fertiliser was refused during the August season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' finds ONAUG across 'season (August)' and 'rejected' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is bird or bat droppings, used as a rich manure.

clue.text: Nudge up one berry

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to jog someone is to nudge them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Give a fruit a push upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns JOG to GOJ.
explanation.definitionFit: The goji is a small red fruit sold dried as a health food.

clue.text: Time and relaxation needed for rib

parts.note: ease is relaxation

explanation.surface: Taking time off to relax is needed for a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib' looks anatomical but is the verb meaning to tease; 'needed for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to make fun of them good-naturedly.

clue.text: Having heavy accents, actors go on air

parts.note: a broad accent is a strong regional one
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A troupe with thick regional accents takes to the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast is to transmit on radio or television.

clue.text: Part of house to attract man getting married?

parts.note: to draw in is to attract
the groom is the man at a wedding

explanation.surface: A room in the home is used to lure a bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split DRAW IN and GROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal sitting room for receiving guests, from withdrawing room.
